A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with readable text, equations, nine tables, 15 figures, and Appendices A–K. The reduction from 18 to 17 pages reflects reflow, including relocation of Appendix K, rather than missing material.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training experiments, loss-scaling analyses, throughput measurements, downstream evaluations, and context-extension experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original training, scaling, throughput, downstream evaluation, and context-extension results, including Tables 4–5 and Appendix J.

M1.justification: Both versions decouple attention-head count from hidden size and jointly optimize model size and GQA configuration using the same candidate selection, scaling-curve fitting, and cost-minimization procedure in Section 4.

E1.justification: Both retain SlimPajama language modeling, the same common-sense evaluation tasks and RULER S-NIAH retrieval tasks, and the same context-length and post-training scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments: MHA and the same GQA configurations in cost analyses, and Llama-3 GQA with H=(32,8) versus H=(8,1) in Table 5.

E3.justification: Table 7 corrects the reported reference configurations used for cost interpolation by changing column headings from N,d,L to N,L,d. For example, the unchanged 1.2B row now correctly denotes L=36 and d=1536, consistent with Table 9. This is a documented-setting correction; training and evaluation procedures otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Head-count analyses, aligned-training-compute comparisons, context-length sensitivity, and the post-training extension experiment in Appendix J.3 are retained unchanged. The new suggestion for broader hyperparameter ablations supplies no additional experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging the final four checkpoints for downstream evaluation in Appendix J.2 and retain the same fitting diagnostics. Run-count, seed, uncertainty, and significance-test reporting practices do not change.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5, plotted results, and fitted coefficients retain their values and findings. For example, Table 5 still reports common-sense accuracy of 45.7% versus 45.5% and inference throughput of 12,921 versus 20,643 tokens/s for Llama-3 GQA versus H=(8,1).

T1.justification: The inference and training cost equations, optimization formulation, scaling functions, and Appendix B reasoning about expected context length are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: context-dependent GQA optimization, fewer heads with larger models for long contexts, and over 50% memory and FLOPs savings without capability degradation. Wording edits do not change their scientific meaning.

C2.justification: v3 adds explicit limitations concerning unablated head dimension, vocabulary size, and model aspect ratio. It also identifies speculative decoding, sparse mixture-of-experts, and hybrid recurrence-attention models as settings requiring further work because they complicate inference-cost calculations.

D1.justification: The first-page availability statement expands from code in v2 to code and models in v3. Table 7 also corrects the layer-count and hidden-size headings. Other implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing, and downstream evaluation instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, Section 2 discussion, and novelty positioning are unchanged. The added references to newer architectural techniques describe applicability limitations without revising comparisons with specific prior works.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited copyedits to the abstract, experimental summaries, and conclusion, consolidates appendix pointers in Section 5.1, updates author information, and adds Acknowledgments. The main section sequence and Appendices A–K remain intact.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained with revised placement and some table styling. Table 5 moves from PDF page 8 to 7, Figure 6 from page 9 to 8, and Appendix K fits onto page 17. Table 7's headings are corrected; plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves qualification and reproducibility documentation through specific new limitations, corrected configuration headings in Table 7, and an expanded code-and-model availability statement. These are useful, limited improvements; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
